Well played this Durham side, who were far too good for Division two almost from the off but never took their feet off the accelerator. They are promoted with nine wins from 12 g ames and not a single defeat. articles.title: Football Daily | Mikel Arteta hits upon a new psychological wheeze for his champions
articles.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! The use of psychological stratagems and pitchside or locker-room sabotage has long been employed by football managers trying to give their teams an edge over visiting rivals.
body: “I love those challenges,” parped Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-season. So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else. Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic, and I don’t want the players, the staff as well, panicking.” Of course, our more astute reader will have already clocked that Arsenal’s flight to Naples this week was delayed by several hours, prompting the cancellation of their pre-match press duties.

body: Defeat to reigning champions Nottinghamshire on Friday left them 32 points from safety with just two fixtures remaining against Leicestershire and Sussex.

"We need to play better cricket and we want to sort of finish this campaign well, it's devastating and it's bottom of the table and it looks dark.

articles.title: Brewers Prospect Achieves Something No Other Player This Century Has
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers are not an organization known for producing many power bats, but rather a team that focuses on developing toolsy players to play their style of baseball. However, Andrew Fischer seems to be an exception.
body: His 47th home run passed Ryan Howard 's 46 Minor League home runs in 2004 with the Philadelphia Phillies organization. Fischer is the first player to reach the 47 home run mark in a Minor League season since Tony Solaita in 1968.
Fischer's historic season is not over yet, as the Brewers' Double-A affiliate, the Biloxi Shuckers, still have four regular-season games left.

Fischer's season ranks fifth all-time in Minor League Baseball's modern era, dating back to 1963. Bill McNulty owns the record with 55 home runs in a single minor league season, followed by Gorman Thomas with 51. Both of those players achieved their respective home run marks in 1974 for Triple-A Sacramento. That season, their home games were played in Hughes Stadium, where the left-field wall was only 233 feet away, per MiLB.com's Michael Avallone.

articles.title: Celtic given 'general behaviour' message by police ahead of Old Firm clash
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill revealed Celtic were given a "general behaviour" warning by Police Scotland ahead of Sunday's League Cup quarter-final against Rangers at Ibrox.
body: There will be no Hoops fans in the 50,000-capacity stadium at the order of the authorities amid a ticket allocation spat between the two Glasgow giants.

The spat is partly a result of the last Old Firm clash in Govan in March, which was marred by fans' disorder as Celtic won the Scottish Gas Scottish Cup quarter-final on penalties after a goalless 120 minutes.

The two clubs have both been ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup matches behind closed doors and have also been handed a £100,000 compensation bill, paid to whichever team is drawn as the away side in their next respective fixtures in that competition.

The 74-year-old Hoops boss admitted that "it'll be a bit strange not having the (Celtic) fans in but I'm nervously and excitedly looking forward to it; it's a great fixture" and also spoke about the police visit.

articles.title: Rams news: LA's bold Australia travel plans bite them in butt
articles.summary: Rams news: LA's bold Australia travel plans bite them in butt appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Los Angeles Rams took one of their worst losses since 2024 in the season opener against the San Francisco 49ers, and some people would put it on…
body: If you look at the game, you can tell who was more prepared, but head coach Sean McVay isn’t going to blame it on the travel plans.

“I don’t believe that that’s why we didn’t play well enough,” McVay said via ESPN’s Nick Wagoner. “I really don’t. … I’ll always make decisions that I think are best for the football team. It’s easy in hindsight to be able to say it was a miss, but those are responsibilities that I’ll take.”

“Win or lose, I know everybody was going to make a big deal about that for either team,” Kyle Shanahan said. “You never know how much that factors into it. You just try to do the best to prepare for 3½ hours. I liked how we prepared, but more importantly, I liked how we played.”

The Rams looked like a team that was trying to find a rhythm all game but never got it. They scored their first and only touchdown in the second quarter, and from there, it was a battle to score any more points.

articles.title: Inside the Solheim Cup: How players embraced 'insane' first-tee experience
articles.summary: Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist said that the Solheim Cup first tee would be 'the place to be in the golfing world,' with that pre-tournament assessment spot on as she witnessed a spectacle unlike any other in the women's game.
body: The horseshoe-shaped grandstand around the first tee at Bernardus Golf was close to capacity long before daylight, with nearly 3,000 spectators - and plenty more along the fairway - creating a party-like atmosphere of noise and excitement.

United States captain Angela Stanford danced onto the tee after emerging from the tunnel, a walk Charley Hull said earlier in the week was like 'entering an arena', with vice-captains - from both sides - doing their best to make things even louder.

One sign on display read 'Dutch courage, European glory', with the Netherlands doing the players proud by creating a boisterous environment more akin to a football stadium or darts event than a golf course.

Nordqvist's vice-captain Anne van Dam grabbed the microphone to guide the crowd through "Links Rechts", the song that became the unofficial anthem for the Dutch football team during the World Cup and involves lots of bouncing in a certain direction.

articles.title: Lowry fires course record to lead Irish Open as McIlroy feels 'frustration'
articles.summary: Shane Lowry broke the course record and raced top of the leaderboard on home soil at the Amgen Irish Open, as Rory McIlroy was left feeling "frustration" in his putting.
body: Lowry mixed nine birdies with a lone bogey during a brilliant eight-under 62 at Trump International Golf Links & Hotel, lifting him to 11 under and three strokes clear of the rest of the morning starters.

The former Open champion's closest challenge from his half of the field came from Haotong Li and Jacob Skov Olesen, who posted rounds of 63 and 64 respectively to move to eight under, with Tom McKibbin among those six strokes back.

Patrick Reed heads into the weekend on four under, with Jon Rahm and Robert MacIntyre another shot adrift, with Rory McIlroy nine off the halfway lead after struggling on the greens during a second successive 69.
First-round leader Joaquin Niemann and England's Tyrrell Hatton were among the later starters.
